series.name: The Interviewer
series.tagline: He asked her why she deserved the job. Her answer made him quit his.
series.concept: A job interviewer — Vikram Mehra, 43, Head of HR — sees hundreds of candidates. Each episode is one interview, both sides. Every interview reveals more about the interviewer than the candidate. Mystery arc: Vikram has an unsigned resignation letter and a son he won't call back.

episodes.title: The First Lie

slides.text: 9:02 AM. Interview Room 3B. Two chairs. One glass table. A jug of water nobody ever drinks. Vikram Mehra, 43, Head of HR, opens Rohit Kapoor's resume. MBA from a tier-2 college. 6-month internship. 'Tell me about yourself.' The most useless question in the world. He asks it anyway.

'I'm a motivated self-starter with strong analytical skills and a passion for—' Vikram holds up a hand. 'Stop. That's from a YouTube video. Top 10 Interview Answers. I've heard it 400 times.' Rohit's face freezes. His entire script just got deleted.

Vikram leans back. 'Tell me something you're bad at. Not "I work too hard." Something you're actually bad at.' 10 seconds of silence. Then Rohit says: 'I'm bad at asking for help. I'd rather fail alone than admit I need someone.'

'Why?' Rohit's jaw tightens. 'Because I'm the first person in my family to get an MBA. If I ask for help, it means the degree wasn't enough. And if the degree wasn't enough...' He doesn't finish. He doesn't need to.

Vikram writes on Rohit's file. Rohit can't see what. The interview continues normally. When Rohit leaves, he notices Vikram's hand paused over a drawer. Inside, briefly visible: a resignation letter. Unsigned.

Vikram sits alone. He looks at the resignation letter. Closes the drawer. Phone buzzes — a name on screen. He declines. Next interview in 8 minutes. He picks up the next resume. Reads a name that makes him pause.

episodes.synopsis: Young MBA graduate Rohit, 24, perfectly rehearsed. Every answer from a YouTube video. Vikram asks one unexpected question. What's underneath the mask is better than the mask.
episodes.caption: He's interviewed 400 people this year. He can spot a rehearsed answer in 3 seconds. But the candidate who told the truth? That answer hit somewhere Vikram didn't expect. What did he write on the file? And whose name is on the next resume?

episodes.title: The Gap

slides.text: 9:30 AM. Meera Sharma sits with perfect posture. Flawless resume — except a black hole. 2021 to 2023. 'Walk me through your career.' She walks through everything. Except those 2 years.

'Tell me about 2021 to 2023.' 'Personal development.' 'What kind?' 'Self-improvement.' 'What skills?' She smiles. 'The kind you can't put on a resume.' She's using corporate language to hide a human story.

Vikram puts down his pen. 'I can't recommend someone who hides 2 years. Not because I think you did something wrong. Because if you can't be honest here, you won't be honest with a team.' The room goes quiet.
'I was a full-time caregiver for my mother. Early-onset Alzheimer's. I bathed her, fed her, stayed up when she wandered at night. She passed in March 2023. I'm here now.'
Vikram doesn't speak for 15 seconds. He opens his drawer. The resignation letter. A face-down photo beside it. He closes the drawer without looking at either.
Vikram smiles — first real smile. 'The gap isn't a gap. It's the most important experience you have.' As she leaves, his phone: 7 missed calls from 'Aarav.' He stares. Doesn't answer.

episodes.synopsis: Meera Sharma, 31, perfect resume with a 2-year gap. She was a full-time caregiver for her mother with Alzheimer's. Her answer forces Vikram to confront his own past.
episodes.caption: She hid 2 years because she was afraid the truth would disqualify her. The truth was she kept her mother alive. Vikram recognized something in her story. What does he know about loss? And who is Aarav?

episodes.title: The Late One

slides.text: 9:45 AM. Scheduled for 9:00. Vikram has written 'NO SHOW.' The door opens. Arjun walks in — shirt untucked, hair uncombed, chai stain. He doesn't look sorry. He looks like caring is something he can't afford.

'Why are you late?' 'Hospital. Father had a seizure at 5 AM. I stayed till they stabilized him.' 'Why not reschedule?' 'Because I've been trying for 8 months. Cancel and I go back to the bottom. I can't afford the bottom again.'
Resume: state college engineering. Startup that shut down. 1 year unemployed. Freelance coding gigs, paying for dialysis. No MBA. No buzzwords. Just survival.

'Client's data pipeline breaks every weekend. Engineering blames client. Client blames us. What do you do?' Without pause: 'Check the logs myself. Everyone's passing blame. The answer is always in the logs.'
Vikram cancels his next two interviews. Spends 40 minutes with Arjun. At 10:25: 'You'll hear from us by Friday.' He means Thursday.
After Arjun leaves, Vikram turns the photo over. For one second: younger Vikram in a hospital, holding someone's hand. Photo goes back down. Phone: Aarav. He almost answers. Almost.

episodes.synopsis: Arjun Nair, 27, 45 minutes late from his father's hospital. Vikram cancels two interviews for him. The photo in the drawer is turned over for the first time.
episodes.caption: 45 minutes late. Chai-stained. Every rule said reject. But the man who can't afford the bottom works hardest to never be there again. What made Vikram cancel two interviews for him?

episodes.title: The Overqualified

slides.text: Priya Rao's resume doesn't fit one page. VP. Board member. 20 years at the top. She applied for: Senior Manager. 'There's been a mistake.' 'No. There hasn't.'
'I spent 20 years climbing. Won everything. Lost my marriage. My daughter's first steps. Her first word. Her first heartbreak. I was in Singapore for all of them.'

'Have you ever wanted to be smaller?' she asks. 'A job that ends at 6? Weekends? Picking up your daughter from school instead of texting sorry from a different time zone?' She's not asking. She's reading him.
'How old is your daughter?' '19. In college.' 'Does she talk to you?' Priya shifts. 'She's learning to. That's why I need a job that lets me be home at 6.'
At the door, she turns: 'Vikram? Whoever is calling you and you're not answering — answer.' She noticed the buzzing phone.
Vikram holds the photo properly. Hospital children's ward. The hand he holds is small. A child's hand. Phone: Aarav. He breathes.

episodes.synopsis: Priya Rao, 46, former VP, applying for mid-level. She traded the corner office for her daughter. She notices Vikram's phone.
episodes.caption: She gave up a VP position to be home by 6. She missed her daughter's childhood. Sometimes the bravest career move is climbing down. And she noticed what nobody else has about Vikram. Who is Aarav?

episodes.title: The Liar

slides.text: 'I single-handedly turned around Q3.' Vikram knows it was a team of 12. He doesn't interrupt. Watching this man lie tells him more than truth would.
Lie 2: 'Left voluntarily.' He was fired. Lie 3: 'Google offer.' Nobody heard from Google. Lie 4: 'Fluent in Mandarin.' His confidence never wavers. That's the interesting part.
'Tell me about a time you failed.' A liar's worst enemy. They have scripts for success. Not failure. Under the mask is where truth lives.
'I micromanaged. I thought I was helping. I was making everyone afraid. They left. One by one. I was let go because I had no team left.' First real sentence.
'I knew about the lies. All of them.' Sunil's face drops. 'But that last answer — that's the person I'd hire. Start again. Real answers. 10 minutes.'
After Sunil leaves, Vikram reads the resignation letter. One line visible: 'I can no longer pretend that this role is what I—' Phone: Aarav. He picks up. 'Hello?' Silence. Click. Aarav hung up.

episodes.synopsis: Sunil Gupta lies on every answer. Vikram lets the house of cards build. When it falls, the truth is more hirable than the lies. Vikram finally answers Aarav's call.
episodes.caption: He lied on every answer. Vikram knew. But he waited for truth to surface. Because truth doesn't need catching — it needs space. Why did Aarav call and hang up?

episodes.title: The Familiar Face

slides.text: Ananya Verma walks in. Handshake. Both freeze for a split second. Vikram KNOWS this face. From life, not a resume. She sits down, eyes on table. She knows exactly where. She won't say.
Standard interview. She's precise but careful. Every answer measured. Not trying to impress. Trying to get through without the conversation going where she fears.
It hits Vikram. The hospital. Three years ago. Children's ward. 'Have we met?' She looks up. 'I was wondering when you'd ask.'
'I was the social worker at the children's hospital. I helped YOUR family.' The room shrinks. 'You talked to your son about cricket scores. None of the other parents talked about normal things.'
'Why did you leave social work?' 'Watching families break. I needed something with less—' 'Less heartbreak?' 'Less memory.' Silence that's not awkward. It's shared.
Photo fully visible: Vikram in hospital, holding hand of a boy with a shaved head. Cricket magazine on the bed. Phone: Aarav. He picks up. 'Dad?' The voice is older. 'I got your letter.'

episodes.synopsis: Ananya was the social worker at the hospital where Vikram's son was treated. She reveals what she remembers. Aarav calls back.
episodes.caption: She recognized him from the hospital. Cricket scores connected a father to his son. Aarav is alive. There's a letter we haven't read yet.

episodes.title: The Father

slides.text: 1:00 PM. No candidate. Vikram eats from a steel tiffin in Interview Room 3B. Two rotis, sabzi, pickle. He eats alone. He always eats alone.
He calls Aarav. 'Hi Dad.' 'You called me 12 times.' 'You didn't answer 12 times.' Then: 'I read your message about the letter. I didn't know how to respond.'

Aarav was 8 when they found leukemia. Vikram spent 7 months in hospital. Read cricket magazines. Talked about Dhoni's captaincy. Aarav survived. The cancer left. So did Vikram's marriage. He hid in work.
Aarav is 22. He sent a handwritten letter: 'Dad, you were there every day in the hospital. Why weren't you there after?' Vikram's read it 30 times. No answer. The resignation letter was his attempt.
'Because I was afraid. When you were sick, I had a purpose. When you got better, I didn't know who to be. So I hid here. Interviewing strangers about their lives because I couldn't face my own.'

Aarav: 'Dad. I'm coming Saturday. India vs Australia. Third test. Want to watch? Like we used to?' Vikram's hand shakes. 'Yeah. I'd like that.' On the table: a cricket magazine. New. He bought it this week.

episodes.synopsis: Vikram's lunch break. No candidate. Through a call to Aarav, we learn everything. Aarav had leukemia. He survived. Vikram didn't — not the same Vikram.
episodes.caption: 7 months reading cricket scores to his son. The son survived. The father hid. 14 years interviewing strangers instead of having the one conversation that mattered. It took a letter to start the healing.

episodes.title: The Second Chance

slides.text: Monday. Vikram walks in different. Shirt less pressed. Tie loose. Two tiffins — one extra. 'In case.' He doesn't glance at the drawer. The photo is face-up.

Rajan Iyer. 55. Resume condensed to one page. Former CFO. Current application: Entry-Level Data Analyst. ₹4 lakh. He once made ₹40 lakh. He sits with the calm of a man who lost everything and survived.
'Business at 50. Failed in 2 years. Lost savings, house. Wife stayed. Kids offered help. I said no. I'd rather start from zero than take from people I should be giving to.'

'Aren't you embarrassed?' Rajan smiles. 'I was. For the first month. Then I realized embarrassment is a luxury for people who haven't actually failed. Once you've hit the ground, there's only the work.'
'I'm not giving you data analyst.' Rajan nods. 'I'm putting you in a different track. Operations mentorship. Someone who's seen top AND bottom.' Rajan's composure breaks into hope.
6 PM. Vikram leaves on time. Texts Aarav: 'Saturday was good. Want to do it again?' Three dots. 'Every Saturday?' He tears the resignation letter in half.

episodes.synopsis: Rajan Iyer, 55, former CFO, applying entry-level. He lost everything in a business failure. Starting over with peace, not desperation. Vikram tears up the resignation letter.
episodes.caption: He lost 40 lakh and applied for 4 lakh. He wasn't embarrassed. He was free. Starting over isn't failure. It's proof you haven't given up. And Vikram tore up the resignation letter.

episodes.title: The Mother

slides.text: Deepa Kumari walks in holding a 6-year-old with pigtails. 'I'm so sorry. My mother fell sick.' Vikram looks at the girl. 'What's your name?' 'Kavya.' 'Want to sit on that chair?' She climbs up.
Deepa is sharp. 5 years customer support. Excellent reviews. She answers while Kavya draws with Vikram's pen. Working twice as hard — proving competent AND a mother.

'How do you handle a screaming customer?' Kavya interrupts: 'Mama talks very softly when people shout. Shouting back makes it louder, not better.' Vikram's note: 'Best answer today. Source: 6-year-old.'
'How do you do it? Single mother, full-time job, no help, and you showed up.' Deepa looks at Kavya. 'Because she's watching. If I give up when it's hard, what am I teaching her?'
'This company has childcare on the 2nd floor. Most people don't know.' Deepa's eyes widen. Kavya waves goodbye. Vikram waves back.
Kavya's drawing: two stick figures at a table. Below: 'My mama is brave.' Vikram pins it to the wall. It stays there every episode after.

episodes.synopsis: Deepa brings her 6-year-old Kavya to the interview. Kavya gives the best answer of the day. Her drawing stays on the wall of 3B forever.
episodes.caption: She brought her daughter to a job interview. Expected to be dismissed. Instead, the 6-year-old gave the best answer. Shouting back makes it louder, not better. Wisdom has no age.

episodes.title: The Record

slides.text: Before Vikram asks anything: 'I spent 3 years in Yerwada Jail for theft. If that disqualifies me, I understand. I just didn't want you to find out later.'

Company policy: criminal record = automatic disqualification. Vikram thinks of the resignation letter he tore up. He chose to stay. What he does from this chair should mean something. 'Tell me what happened.'

'Mother needed surgery. No bank lends to a man with no collateral and 12,000 salary. I stole stock from the warehouse. Not proud. Not looking for sympathy. I want a chance to work where I don't have to steal to survive.'

Vikram calls the HR director. 'Policy says no.' 'I know. I'm asking if you SHOULD approve it.' 'Your job is to follow policy.' 'My job is to hire the right people. Sometimes policy and the right person don't align.'
Subject: Exception Request — Manoj Patil. Note: 'This man told me the truth before I asked. That's rarer than a clean record.'
Wednesday. One-line reply: 'Exception approved. Probation. 6 months. Your responsibility.' Vikram forwards to Manoj. Goes home on time. Second week in a row.

episodes.synopsis: Manoj, 3 years in prison for theft, discloses before being asked. Vikram fights company policy. Exception approved.
episodes.caption: Criminal record. Told the truth before anyone asked. Policy said reject. Conscience said listen. What do you do when the right thing and the rules disagree?

episodes.title: The Last Interview

slides.text: 6:00 PM. Interview Room 3B. Vikram is in the candidate chair. Across: Aarav, 22, his father's jawline. 'Hi Dad.' 'Hi.' 'I have some questions.' His folder is empty. He doesn't need notes.
'Tell me about yourself.' Vikram laughs. The most useless question. 'I'm 43. I work in HR.' 'That's your resume. I asked about you.' His own technique, aimed at him.

'I'm a man who sat in a hospital for 7 months talking about cricket because he didn't know how to talk about cancer. When you got better, I didn't know what to talk about. So I talked to strangers instead.'

'The question from my letter. You were there every day in the hospital. Why weren't you there after?' 'Because I was afraid that if I stayed close, I'd lose you again. And I wouldn't survive it twice.'
'Dad. You told me about every interview. The mother with the 6-year-old. The man who started over at 55. You see the best in strangers. I just wanted you to see it in us.'
Vikram hugs his son. In Interview Room 3B. Next to Kavya's drawing, he pins Aarav's letter. The water jug — Aarav picks it up and pours a glass. Someone finally drinks from it.

episodes.synopsis: Vikram sits in the candidate's chair. Aarav sits behind the desk. The question isn't about a job. It's about a life.
episodes.caption: 25 interviews. 25 strangers. And the one person he couldn't interview — himself. Until his son asked the only question that mattered. The answer took 14 years. But it came.
